cause: CPU srsUE NR RLC receiver fails to normalize a received segment that fully contains an existing segment, then misclassifies overlapping bytes as a missing interval while generating a STATUS NACK.
code_path: handle_data_pdu checks whether either incoming endpoint lies inside a stored segment, but does not detect an incoming range that fully contains a stored segment.
insert_received_segment inserts both ranges, sorted by start offset.
get_status_pdu handles any segment start differing from last_so as a missing gap, without distinguishing overlap.
After [656,764], last_so is765; the stored [684,695] then produces NACK [765,683].
The interval-order assertion aborts the UE; the broker subsequently stops after missing that UE IQ.

reproduction.library: Unmodified libsrsran_rlc.a from the CPU UE build
reproduction.headers: 18-bit SN617, middle segments; lengths and offsets match the captured live packets
reproduction.payload: Zero-filled synthetic bytes; range handling does not inspect payload values

outer_first.result: Duplicate detected and STATUS generation completes

interpretation: The arrival/overlap pattern is sufficient to trigger the bug without multi-UE CPU load, gNB affinity changes or GPU execution. The experiment does not establish which earlier loss, ACK timing or scheduling event caused those live retransmissions.
repair_direction: Normalize overlapping received byte ranges while preserving newly received bytes, and generate STATUS NACKs from actual missing intervals; keep the receive frontier monotonic.
changes: Diagnostic reproduction only. No UE/gNB/channel production source or binary changed; no application fix applied.
